topic: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate (SAA-C04) exam preparation - the current 2026 version of AWS's flagship associate cloud-architecture certification, built around designing secure, resilient, high-performing, and cost-optimized AWS solutions
exam_format: 65 questions (50 scored + 15 unscored), 130 minutes, passing score 720 out of 1000 (scaled), delivered online-proctored or at a Pearson VUE test center. Question types are multiple choice (one correct answer of four) and multiple response (two or more correct of five or more). SAA-C04 is the CURRENT version (released March 2024, replacing SAA-C03) and remains current in 2026. Certification is valid for 3 years.
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) and multiple response clearly marked as 'Select TWO/THREE'
audience: Cloud engineers, solutions architects, developers, sysadmins, and IT professionals designing and deploying systems on AWS. Candidates should have roughly one year of hands-on AWS experience and familiarity with core services. A strong companion and feeder to the AWS AI Practitioner (AIF-C01) and AWS GenAI Developer (AIP-C01) courses in this catalog.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Design Secure Architectures
domains.notes: The largest domain (up from C03 - security weight increased in C04). Secure access to AWS resources: IAM users, groups, roles, policies, permission boundaries, identity federation, IAM Identity Center (SSO), AWS Organizations SCPs, resource-based vs identity-based policies, least privilege, root-account protection, MFA. Secure workloads and applications: security groups vs network ACLs, VPC design, public/private subnets, NAT gateways, VPC endpoints (gateway/interface), PrivateLink, AWS WAF, Shield, Network Firewall, Security Hub, GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie. Data security: encryption at rest and in transit, KMS (customer-managed vs AWS-managed keys, key rotation, grants), CloudHSM, Secrets Manager vs Systems Manager Parameter Store, ACM/TLS, S3 bucket policies, block public access, S3 encryption options. Emphasis on choosing the right control for a described requirement.

domains.name: Design Resilient Architectures
domains.notes: Design scalable and loosely coupled architectures: decoupling with SQS, SNS, EventBridge, Step Functions, API Gateway; fan-out patterns; microservices; container (ECS/EKS/Fargate) and serverless (Lambda) designs; event-driven architectures; caching. Design highly available and fault-tolerant architectures: Multi-AZ vs Multi-Region, Auto Scaling groups, Elastic Load Balancing (ALB/NLB/GWLB) and target groups, Route 53 routing policies (failover, latency, weighted, geolocation) and health checks; RTO/RPO and backup/restore, pilot light, warm standby, multi-site active-active; S3 durability and versioning, cross-region replication; RDS Multi-AZ and read replicas, Aurora, DynamoDB global tables; disaster-recovery strategy selection for a given RTO/RPO.

domains.name: Design High-Performing Architectures
domains.notes: High-performing storage: S3 storage classes and performance, EBS volume types (gp3, io2), instance store, EFS vs FSx, S3 Transfer Acceleration, storage for different access patterns. High-performing compute: EC2 instance families and sizing, Auto Scaling policies, Lambda concurrency and sizing, containers, Elastic/placement groups, Graviton. High-performing networking: global acceleration (CloudFront, Global Accelerator), Direct Connect vs VPN, VPC peering vs Transit Gateway, edge networking. High-performing databases: choosing RDS vs Aurora vs DynamoDB vs ElastiCache vs Redshift, read replicas, DAX, connection pooling (RDS Proxy). Data ingestion/processing at scale: Kinesis, Data Firehose, Glue, EMR, Athena. Choosing the most performant option for a scenario is the core skill.

domains.name: Design Cost-Optimized Architectures
domains.notes: Cost-optimized storage: S3 lifecycle policies, Intelligent-Tiering, Glacier tiers, EBS/EFS/S3 cost trade-offs, data-transfer cost awareness. Cost-optimized compute: EC2 pricing models (On-Demand, Reserved Instances, Savings Plans, Spot, Dedicated), right-sizing, Auto Scaling for cost, serverless vs always-on, Compute Optimizer. Cost-optimized databases and networking: choosing managed vs self-managed, caching to cut cost, minimizing NAT/data-transfer charges, VPC endpoints to avoid egress. Cost governance and visibility: AWS Budgets, Cost Explorer, Cost and Usage Report, Trusted Advisor, tagging and allocation, consolidated billing via Organizations. Picking the lowest-cost design that still meets requirements is the recurring exam pattern.

extra_guidance: SAA-C04 is the flagship, highest-traffic AWS associate certification - the strongest volume play in the catalog. CRITICAL freshness angle: this course is built for the CURRENT SAA-C04 (released March 2024), while many competing Udemy courses are still on the retired/older SAA-C03 - lead the marketing with 'updated for the CURRENT SAA-C04, not the old C03.' The four domain names and weights above are AWS's official SAA-C04 exam-guide domains - use them verbatim. Key C04 shift to reflect: security weight rose to 30% (the single largest domain), so give security-first architecture extra depth. This is a design/decision exam, NOT a hands-on console exam - the skill is choosing the BEST AWS service or pattern for a described requirement under constraints (cost, latency, availability, security), so practice questions MUST be scenario-based with plausible distractors and 'BEST/MOST cost-effective/MOST highly available' framing. Cover the classic decision pairs relentlessly: security groups vs NACLs, gateway vs interface VPC endpoints, ALB vs NLB, SQS vs SNS vs EventBridge, RDS vs Aurora vs DynamoDB, EBS vs EFS vs FSx vs instance store, Reserved vs Savings Plans vs Spot, Multi-AZ vs Multi-Region, Direct Connect vs VPN, CloudFront vs Global Accelerator, Cognito vs IAM. Labs are architecture-diagram walkthroughs and console tours at read-and-understand level (VPC build, Auto Scaling + ALB, S3 lifecycle, IAM policy read), not deep CLI. Funnel note: reference that learners can go deeper on AWS AI with the AIF-C01 and AIP-C01 courses. Final chapter must be a full exam simulation with a 130-minute time-management strategy for 65 questions and guidance on multiple-response elimination. Scan the practice bank for other-vendor terms (Azure/GCP) before upload per the pipeline compliance rules.
